name: Aptamer-Drug Conjugate (ApDC)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Deliver a cytotoxic or therapeutic payload to specific cells by conjugating it to an RNA aptamer that binds a cell-surface protein on the target cell type.
molecularDefect: Diseases requiring targeted drug delivery to specific cell populations, particularly cancers and autoimmune diseases.
diseaseMechanism: An RNA aptamer binds a cell-surface marker specific to the target cell type (e.g., tumor-associated antigen). A therapeutic payload (cytotoxic drug, siRNA, or immunomodulator) is chemically conjugated to the aptamer. The aptamer internalizes upon binding, delivering the payload selectively to target cells while sparing normal tissue.
suitableVariantTypes: Cancers with defined surface markers; autoimmune diseases with pathogenic cell populations; any disease requiring cell-type-specific drug delivery.
typicalDiseases: Hematologic malignancies (CD30+ lymphoma); solid tumors (PSMA+ prostate cancer); autoimmune diseases (CD20+ B cells). Preclinical and early clinical.
rnaTargetRegion: Not applicable (targets cell-surface proteins rather than RNA).
typicalLength: Aptamer: 30-80 nt; linker: variable; payload: variable (drug, siRNA, etc.).
designRules: Select aptamer against cell-surface marker via SELEX; optimize internalization efficiency; design conjugation chemistry (click chemistry, disulfide bond, thiol-maleimide); validate payload delivery and efficacy in vitro.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Essential. Aptamer must maintain binding structure after conjugation.
offTargetConsiderations: Off-target delivery to cells expressing low levels of the target marker; payload toxicity to normal tissues; aptamer degradation in serum.
advantages: Targeted delivery reduces systemic toxicity; aptamers have low immunogenicity; modular design allows different payloads; can be engineered for controlled release.
limitations: Aptamer stability in serum requires chemical modification; conjugation chemistry may affect binding; internalization efficiency varies; limited clinical validation.
fdaApprovedDrugs: None (bexarotene and other targeted therapies use antibody conjugates, not aptamer conjugates)
clinicalTrialExamples: AS1411 (nucleolin-targeting aptamer in cancer); no approved aptamer-drug conjugates.

evidenceLevel.note: Preclinical proof-of-concept in several cancer models; no clinical-stage aptamer-drug conjugates.
